title: How can the boatman carry all three across without a meal?
description: Sanju and Mira are on a train and Mira poses the river crossing puzzle. The video finds the one animal that cannot be left with either of the others, and plans the trips.
teaching_notes: One idea: find who is in both risky pairs, take it first, and bring it back when needed. Watch for children who take the biggest animal first.

source: How can the boatman take the lion, the sheep and the grass a
video_script.why: The child has met the puzzle but has not yet seen that one passenger sits in both risky pairs and so decides the order.
video_script.substitution: Sort the pairs into safe and unsafe, take the one in both unsafe pairs first, then bring it back once.
video_script.anchor: Sanju and Mira on a train, with Mira's river puzzle drawn on a card between them
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu takes the lion first because it is biggest, which leaves the sheep alone with the grass.

final_answer.value: 7 crossings: sheep, back, lion, sheep back, grass, back, sheep

never_show: the your-turn answer, the hen first
maths_rules: risky pairs when alone: sheep with grass, lion with sheep; safe pair: lion with grass
the sheep is in both risky pairs, so it crosses first
trip 1 sheep across; trip 2 back empty; trip 3 lion across; trip 4 sheep back; trip 5 grass across; trip 6 back empty; trip 7 sheep across
7 crossings in all; after trip 3 the grass waits alone on the near shore, and after trip 4 the sheep waits with the grass and the boatman
slip: lion first leaves the sheep with the grass
your turn: fox eats hen, hen eats corn; the hen is in both risky pairs, so the hen goes first; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: the animal in both risky pairs goes first. Wrong idea: take the biggest first. A river with two shores stays on the stage, and the trips are listed on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='train'/>Sanju and Mira travel on a train, and Mira sets a puzzle.
<bookmark mark='crew'/>A boatman must take a lion, a sheep and a bundle of grass across a river.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The boat carries only one of them at a time.
<bookmark mark='eat'/>Left alone, the sheep eats the grass, and the lion eats the sheep.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can he take all three across safely, in the fewest trips?

narration: <bookmark mark='pairs'/>Look at the three pairs that may be left alone on a shore.
<bookmark mark='bad1'/>The sheep and the grass cannot stay alone, because the sheep eats the grass.
<bookmark mark='bad2'/>The lion and the sheep cannot stay alone, because the lion eats the sheep.
<bookmark mark='safe'/>The lion and the grass are safe together, because a lion does not eat grass.
<bookmark mark='who'/>One animal is in both red pairs, and it is the sheep.
